full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This Rule is directed against the order dated 27-5-87 passed by the learned Munsif, Gournadi in Miscellaneous case No.52 of 1986 under Order 9 rule 9 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit and restoring the same to its original file and number. 

 2. The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted a suit in the 6th Court of Munsif. Barisal being Title Suit No.479 of 1994, for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No.244 of 1973 is illegal, void and not binding upon them, Subsequently, the suit was transferred to the 2nd Court of Munsif, Barisal and was renumbered as Title Suit No.205 of 1978. Eventually the plaint was amended and the plaintiffs added a prayer for declaration of their title in the suit land. In course of time the said suit was transferred to the Court of the Munsif, Gournadi and re-numbered as Title Suit No.47 of 1985. It is gathered from the records that this suit was decreed on contest. On appeal the judgment of the trial Court was reversed and the case was sent back on remand to the trial Court for a fresh trial in accordance with law and in the light of the observations made in the body of the judgment after the suit was sent back on remand the learned Munsif directed the Sheristradar to assess the valuation of the suit and fixed several dates for taking necessary steps by the plaintiffs. The defendants rasised objection on the valuation of the suit whereupon the learned Munsif passed an order for taking steps by the plaintiffs but on a number of dates fixed for the purpose the plaintiffs remained absent and failed to take steps directed by the Court Eventually on 3-7-86 the plaintiffs were asked to show cause by 20-7-86 as to why the suit shall not be dismissed for not taking necessary steps. On 20-7-86 the plaintiffs failed to show cause following which the suit was dismissed for default. Against the aforesaid order of dismissal the plaintiff-opposite parties filed an application under Order 9 rule 9 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the dismissal of the suit for default on the ground that the show-cause notice in question did not specify the steps they were required to take and they were thus confused about their duty in pursuance of the order of the Court and the same prevented them from taking the desired steps. Under such circumstances, the plaintiffs expressed regrets and prayed for setting aside the order of dismissal in the interest of justice. The learned Munsif by his impugned order dated 27-5-87 set aside the ex parte dismissal of the suit and restored the same to its original file and number on payment of Taka 100.00 as cost to the defendants. It is against this order the defendant-petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the learned Munsif erred in law in passing the impugned order in disregard of the provision of Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the learned Munsif erred in law in failing to apply his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 6. In support of his submission the learned Advocate for the opposite parties has referred to me the case of Rafiqul Islam and another vs. Abul Kalam and ors reported in 42 DLR 19. The principle of law enunciated in the cited decision fully applies to the facts and circumstances of the present case and I am in respectful agreement with the principle of law enunciated therein. 

 8. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 27-5-87 passed by the learned Munsif, Gournadi in Miscellaneous Case No. 52 of 1986 is affirmed. 

 9. The order of Stay earlier granted by this Court stands vacated. In view of the fact that this is a very old case, the interest of justice demands that it be disposed of with utmost expediency.
